headline: Musk's 'guppy-level death' warning and a record CoreWeave debt cost turned the AI worry from demand to who can still borrow: neoclouds -31% on the month while ai_software rose 9.2% in five days.
regime: The AI-bottleneck complex is still in a financing-driven drawdown: the semis ETF is -12.2% on the month and -2.3% over five days, with grid (-9.5% 5d), networking/optical (-9.0%) and power (-7.6%) hit hardest, even though semis ticked up 0.7% today. The 10-year yield sits at 4.99% with crude at $101 and a Fed meeting this week, so the discount rate stays high, and the VIX is up 20.7% on the month. Only ai_software (+9.2% 5d) is rising, which is rotation away from capital-heavy infrastructure, not confirmation of the build-out. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report this week and will decide whether capex is funded.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Constellation signed a 3,590 MW package with Google including 890 MW of new nuclear uprates (57003b30755d)
GE Vernova's gigawatts of gas power matter more than its backlog going into Oct. 28 earnings (79fa3a2ff8d4)
Grid fell 9.5% over five days (PWR -13.5%) and Vistra is -17% in three months despite a $4.2B nuclear loan offer, so the market is pricing financing, not scarcity (5526686953fd)
theses.change_note: Physical demand evidence (Google deals) offsets price weakness; neither side moved enough to change confidence.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Wedbush calls Super Micro's preliminary Q1 results a clear positive (2457ac26ffe1)
AMD's Helios rack blueprint is signing Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE and Supermicro (5845e440b484)
Against: Nvidia has effectively lost China and Musk expects half-built data centres as debt markets shut (6defdfbb9bec, fb65ef6c8104)
theses.change_note: -4: order signals are thin today and the counter-evidence is about who can pay, which is the same funding risk.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave is down 38% in October and its debt costs hit a record while SpaceX borrows $40B (52aa20b40d88, 10dcc7fcaa17)
Nebius's CEO admits asset-backed and debt financing has tightened (19dc6de4b8ea)
Cipher Digital fell 30% after a zero-coupon note sale despite a $9B backlog (321b691362f3)
theses.change_note: +4: the segment is -31.1% on the month and the stress is now visible in bond pricing and a second issuer, not just equity.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Micron is still up 208% in 2026 with quarterly revenue more than doubled (9b50bcf74f21)
The segment is down 25.6% on the month, so the multiple has already compressed (digest tape)
Seagate reports tomorrow and is the next test of storage demand (22fd203f597c)
theses.change_note: No new fundamental data; Seagate's print tomorrow is the next test.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Meta is raising $35B for AI and creating a new share class so Zuckerberg can raise capital without giving up votes (e271c0e808cb, 194c5b114e32)
Oracle's record AI backlog sits against a stretched balance sheet (a86f68b79f86)
Meta is -9.4% over five days (digest tape)
theses.change_note: +2: funding is now external and dilutive of control, but Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings this week could change the picture.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: The bond market is warning tech investors of more poundings (79fe7960d360)
The 10-year is 4.99% with oil at $101 and a Fed hiking cycle in the background (76043034d9e0, 98e6da7732fb)
Semis ETF -12.2% and VIX +20.7% on the month (digest tape)
theses.change_note: +2: yields touched 5% and a Fed decision is due this week.

compute.note: -15.0% on the month; AMD's rack blueprint helps but Nvidia's China loss and funding risk cap it.

foundry_equipment.note: -7.1% over five days (LRCX -12.8%); cyclical and crowded.

memory_storage.note: -25.6% on the month on single-digit forward P/Es; Seagate reports tomorrow.

networking_optical.note: -9.0% over five days (FN -13.4%), -22.6% on the month; no valuation cushion.

servers.note: Supermicro and Jabil show steady demand; Celestica -14.4% over five days shows the risk.

power_nuclear.note: Google deals back demand; stick to cash-generating producers, not pre-revenue nuclear.

grid_electrical.note: -9.5% over five days is financing fear on an intact bottleneck; Hubbell reports tomorrow, GE Vernova Oct. 28.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv closed a services acquisition; -6.5% over five days with TT the best at -3.0%.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -31.1% on the month with record debt costs; avoid until financing clears.

hyperscalers.note: Capex now needs outside funding; wait for Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.

ai_software.note: +9.2% over five days is rotation and momentum, not a bottleneck play.

risks: Neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave, Nebius, Cipher) could spread to GPU, power and cooling suppliers through cancelled or delayed orders.
A hawkish Fed this week with the 10-year at 4.99% would extend the multiple compression in crowded AI names.
Hyperscaler earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet Wed; Amazon Thu) could cut capex guidance and hit the whole supplier chain.
Oil at $101 on Middle East tension keeps inflation and rate risk elevated.
Memory earnings may be at peak cycle after Micron's 208% year-to-date gain.
watch: Seagate and Teradyne results tomorrow, and Hubbell's report, for storage, test and grid demand.
Fed decision this week and whether the 10-year holds under 5%.
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon capex commentary Wednesday and Thursday.
GE Vernova on Oct. 28 for gigawatts of gas power orders.
CoreWeave bond yields and whether other neoclouds can raise debt.
monday_note: Digest-only sketch gave five of the six theses on today's evidence (neocloud credit, capex funding, high rates, power backed by Google deals, memory compression). ai-demand-exceeds-supply is the one that mostly survives by carry-forward: today's digest has only Supermicro and AMD order signals against clear funding counter-evidence.
